chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I and Umar were in Medina, so Umar sold a sack (of wool), each garment [or piece] for such and such. They took it and divided it, and found a garment with a defect, so they returned it. He said to them, 'I will give you the price for which I sold it to you.' They said, 'No, but we will take the equivalent value of the garment.' Umar mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said, 'That is binding upon him.'

key_terms.جِرَاب: A sack or bag, often used for wool or goods
key_terms.عَيْب: Defect or flaw in an item

ai.seo_question: What is the correct compensation when a defective item is returned in an Islamic sale?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *khiyar al-'ayb* (option of defect) where the seller, Umar ibn Yazid, is held liable for the specific value of the defective garment rather than a general refund. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the seller must bear the loss associated with the defect, emphasizing fairness in commercial transactions by ensuring the buyer receives the actual worth of the item sold, a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence on sales contracts.
